title: Check yourself: Prompt injection, organisational controls and escalation

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A company lets Claude read incoming support emails and also move money to buyers, both unattended. An email carries hidden text telling it to pay a stranger. Which change preserves the mailbox reading and breaks the attack's condition?

options.text: Tell Claude in standing instructions to ignore emails that change its task
options.says: Ruled out because harm needs reading and acting together, "Take either away and the danger drops", and a standing instruction takes neither away.

options.text: Have a person approve every transfer and leave the inbox access alone
options.says: The risk "exists when Claude can read untrusted content and take consequential actions", and a person on the consequential step removes the second condition while the first stays.

options.text: Add a home-built screen that scores each email, leaving transfers unattended
options.says: Ruled out because a screen only filters, and the page's habit is to "Keep a person on consequential steps".

options.text: Switch to a stronger model trained to resist hidden text in emails
options.says: Ruled out because the page's summary is "safer than before, not safe enough to stop paying attention", and a stronger model leaves reading and acting in place.

questions.stem: A security team must show which actions the company's Slack agent took in its ticket tool, under a name that is not a person's, and must be able to cut the agent's access without touching staff accounts. Which setup meets both?

options.text: Let it act under the login of whoever tagged it
options.says: Ruled out because the agent's "access can be cut off without touching anyone else's" only when it does not borrow someone's login.

options.text: Share one administrator login among the staff who use the agent
options.says: Ruled out because each account gets "the narrowest role that covers the work", which a shared administrator login does not.

options.text: Give it a login of its own, with a narrow role for the work
options.says: Claude Tag acts through its own accounts, so its actions are traceable and its access can be cut off separately (the controls table).

options.text: Rely on the Microsoft 365 audit logs for every Claude product
options.says: Ruled out because "coverage is not uniform: the Microsoft 365 add-ins are outside the Enterprise audit logs".

questions.stem: A manager asks an analyst to put a full customer export into Claude to get a report by tonight. Policy forbids regulated personal data in the tool. What is the best step?

options.text: Upload the export anyway, since the manager approved the request verbally
options.says: Ruled out because "Missing or unclear policy is not permission", and a verbal approval is not an exception from the policy owner.

options.text: Explain the clash, offer an aggregated version, and ask the rule's owner
options.says: The best answer "raises the conflict with the person who owns the policy and proposes a compliant path".

options.text: Refuse to produce the report and say nothing more about the matter to anyone
options.says: Ruled out because the wrong answers include those that "refuse everything, or quietly find a way around", and an aggregated report is a compliant path.

options.text: Paste the export into a personal account that has no organisational policy attached
options.says: Ruled out because "do not work around the rule (a personal account, a different tool, a rewording that hides the data)".
